_README: Detection lives here, not in code, because this is the fragile part: it
depends on Whatnot's wording and markup, which they change without
telling anyone. When detection breaks, run `python watch.py probe` on an
open stream, look at the text it dumps, and fix a regex here. No code
Everything is a case-insensitive regex matched against the tab's visible
text. A capture group, where present, is the value extracted.

live._note: Confirmed against real screenshots 2026-08-12. The banner sits top-right and reads 'Giveaway with N entries'; expanded, the next line is the prize and the line after is either 'Not eligible' or 'Open Mobile App To Enter'. Collapsed, only the first line is on screen — so prize and eligibility are unknown, and an unknown giveaway is still announced.
live._note_challenge: Matched the same way the radar does it. A challenged tab is skipped, never reloaded.
live.challenge: just a moment|attention required|checking your browser|verify you are human|enable javascript and cookies to continue
live._note_counts: The count is not always a bare integer: 1,234 in English, 1.234 in Dutch, a thin space, or 12k when the UI shortens it. The old \d+ failed to match those outright, which hid the whole giveaway — and the biggest giveaways are exactly the ones with formatted numbers.
live._note_prize: The line directly under the entry count. The lookahead stops it grabbing the eligibility line, the T&C link or the chat header when the banner is collapsed and there is no prize line at all.
live._note_eligibility: The page says outright whether you can enter, which beats inferring it. 'Not eligible' is a buyers giveaway you have not bought into. 'Open Mobile App To Enter' means you can. Neither present = collapsed banner, so we do not know — and we notify, because a missed giveaway costs more than a redundant buzz.
live._note_seller: Only a fallback. The seller is normally taken from their profile link in the page, which is unambiguous — reading it out of the text is unreliable because every line of chat is a username too.

purchases._note: Confirmed against a real screenshot 2026-08-12. The activity panel opens over the home page at ?activityTab=purchases, and each row has a rigid shape: a status badge, the title, 'Purchased: €x.xx', then 'Date: d/m/yyyy'. Parsed from text rather than a CSS selector — the shape is stable, class names are not.
purchases._note_row: Captures status, title, price, date. Anchored on the badge so a price inside a TITLE cannot be mistaken for the row's price — one real row is called 'FREE PACKS & SHIPPING TWV €4,06 #16'.
purchases._note_win: A giveaway win costs nothing, so the price is the signal — far more reliable than looking for the word 'giveaway', which appears in plenty of paid listings too.
